A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SWIFT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding experiments, including benchmark results in Tables 2–6, domain-shift evaluations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds 70B-model evaluations and comparisons of acceleration and optimization costs in Appendix C.2 and D.3–D.4.

M1.justification: The two-stage algorithm and confidence-aware verification remain unchanged. However, v2 Appendix C.2 reports a limited procedural adaptation for LLaMA-3-70B: automatically reducing the skip ratio from 0.5 to 0.4 when acceptance remains below 0.7, extending v1's stated fixed-ratio procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same summarization, reasoning, storytelling, code generation, translation, instruction-following, and question-answering coverage. The added model evaluations and optimization-budget comparisons use existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: v1 compares principally with Parallel and Lookahead, while evaluating Self-SD in preliminary and domain-shift analyses. v2 Tables 10–12 add direct CNN/DM comparisons with LayerSkip and Self-SD augmented with dynamic verification, substantially expanding evaluation against closely related alternatives.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA-2-70B-Chat and LLaMA-3-70B base/instruction evaluations, including a 0.4 skip ratio for LLaMA-3. Appendix D.4 introduces optimization-budget controls and a reduced-data Self-SD setting using one eight-token sample instead of eight 32-token samples. Existing main benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3–D.4 analyses examine acceleration versus optimization cost, including a latency–speedup curve, similar-budget comparisons, and reduced-sample Self-SD controls. These substantially extend investigation of the optimization contribution. Existing context-window, domain-shift, scaling, and case-study analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains the same ± latency reporting. v2 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds 70B-model results and baseline/cost results in Tables 5 and 10–12. The dynamic-verification ablation also changes: v1 Table 7 reports M=5.72, acceptance=0.98, and speedup=1.541×; v2 Table 8 reports 4.39, 0.90, and 1.342×. Full SWIFT remains at 1.560×. Main Tables 2–4 retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the matchness definition, optimization formulation, and expected-speedup derivation are retained. The new optimization-complexity discussion adds no formal theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: task-specific layer sparsity, training-free on-the-fly self-speculative decoding, and approximately 1.3×–1.6× acceleration while preserving the target output distribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets differing LLaMA-2/LLaMA-3 skip ratios as model-dependent redundancy and adds specific applicability arguments concerning unsupported checkpoints and small workloads. It also argues that retraining early-exit models may affect output reliability. The original sparsity, scaling, and adaptation interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies details for the added evaluations, including optimization sample/token budgets, iteration counts, timing attribution, and the LLaMA-3 acceptance threshold. The existing software/hardware setup, general inference settings, and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix D.5–D.6 substantially expands positioning against training-dependent early-exit and non-autoregressive drafting methods, including computational-cost and deployment arguments. Four cited works are added: Bae et al., Hooper et al., Yang et al., and Kim et al. The original novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: v2 condenses parts of the abstract and introduction, adds acknowledgements and the conference-publication header, and inserts appendix subsections with updated cross-references. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an expanded 70B-results table, three tables displaying baseline performance and optimization costs, and a latency–speedup figure. Existing displays are repositioned or resized, while the layer-configuration visualization and case studies are retained under new numbering. The additions substantially expand the comparative displays.

improvement.justification: v1 lacks direct LayerSkip and budget-controlled Self-SD comparisons. v2 addresses this important gap through Tables 10–12 and Figure 11, including dynamically augmented Self-SD controls that help distinguish optimization benefits from verification benefits. This substantially strengthens assessment of the central efficiency contribution; the additional 70B evaluations further support applicability. The unexplained ablation revision limits confidence in that particular change, but the overall improvement rests on the stronger comparative evidence.
